subject: Money
title: Money Supply and Printing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Money Supply and Printing.

hook.text: The U.S. created 40% of all dollars in existence between 2020 and 2021. Four out of ten dollars are brand new.

buildup.text: Quantitative easing: the Fed buys bonds, adding money to banks. Banks lend more, money multiplies through the economy.

discovery.text: More money doesn't cause inflation if it stays in banks. It only inflates prices when it reaches consumers and is spent.

twist.text: After 2008, the Fed printed trillions but inflation stayed low. The money went to asset markets, not grocery stores.

climax.text: After 2020, stimulus checks went straight to consumers. This time, the money hit Main Street and prices followed.

punchline.text: Printing money isn't inflation. Spending it is.

quiz.question: Why didn't massive money printing after 2008 cause high consumer inflation?
options: The money went to asset markets, not consumers
